notes: Units were matched by passage and rule, not by anchor alone (three of coder A's anchors sat on the wrong sample statement but its policy text matched coder B's unit). Main disagreements: (1) actor (all vs admin vs student vs instructor) for rationale and informs sentences, resolved by who the sentence addresses (second person means student, page addressed to instructors means instructor, general rationale means all); (2) phase, mostly before-course vs general/course-start/over-time, resolved by whether the sentence sets up policy, states a principle, or communicates it; (3) policy_type, e.g. P21 vs P19, P05 vs P04 for the stoplight and tier descriptions (resolved to P05), P24 vs P26 within the appendix list, P05/P85 for the graduate templates sentence (resolved to P110), and P24/P63/P09 for pointers to examples and icons (resolved to P110 and P115); (4) modality 'is expected' read as must, 'consider' as should, permission statements as may, and consequences as informs; (5) unit_stance for citation and record-keeping procedures set to neutral. Single-coder units were checked against the source text: 9 of A's and 10 of B's were kept as real statements. Dropped: A's duplicate student unit on searching for examples, A's lump unit listing the graduate policy elements (kept as separate units from B), B's repeat of the responsibility sentence, and B's detector-evolution prediction. Coder UNCOVERED notes were kept; none were mapped to an existing type. No new types were proposed.
